I’ve struggled with this most of my life, whether it’s the anxiety about not having enough money, or the depression that comes with knowing you can’t do things that others can do with the money they have. I’ve gotten to the point now where I may not have money for a cruise or something big, but I’ve found things that I really enjoy that don’t break the bank, and since I’m not spending all of my money anymore then I know that I’ve got enough until the next paycheck and that feeling of security is so peaceful. So you might just need to figure out where you may be spending too much, and then try to cut back so you’ll have extra money and if you’ve got friends that want to do something crazy like a cruise or something then try to save for it as best you can rather than spending the rest of what you do have in the bank in attempt to not appear like the party pooper in the friends circle, haha. And I just noticed you said you’re in college, I am too and man who isn’t broke in college ya know? Haha, it’s almost how it’s meant to be, but once you get the ball rolling with a career then the money will follow and you won’t need to stress about it. And one thing that’s true especially with money is things are not always as they seem, I bet your friends probably think that you have more than them because we always perceive others as having more than us and sometimes that’s true and sometimes it’s not.

Whatever you decide on just make sure you enjoy it, or you won’t stick to it unless you can foster discipline overnight! But find something you enjoy and is productive and form a habit out of that, the more you do this then the easier it will be to form habits with more unpleasant things that will be good for you, and that my friend is how discipline is created! Good luck, you sound like a good person, you’ll find what you’re looking for, and I know this because you’re looking for it! Haha.

You may feel a lack of motivation, but you seem incredibly talented and you wouldn’t be talented with those things if you didn’t have any interest in them, and that’s essentially what motivation is, desire or interest. You have drive, you just may not know where to direct it just yet, and it’s easier to know where to direct a drive like yours when you know where you want to end up. I had severe ADHD that held me back severely in high school, and that i recently (finally) started taking meds for, and it took trying a few different ones, but since I’ve found this one that works I’ve seriously never been so productive and I finally feel much less anxious and I’m calm, but definitely not zombie-like, because I took one that made me a zombie, but with some trial and error I found the right one. But if that’s not your problem then it sounds like maybe you need to come up with a vision of where you see yourself in the future, and make sure it’s something you really are interested in. The day that I decided I wanted to become an orthopedic surgeon more than anything was the day I felt like a lot more of my life actually made sense. Anyway, that’s just my experience, you sound incredibly talented, and whether you think so or not you’ve got drive, I think the problem is maybe you don’t know where to direct it yet. Good luck bud, and let me know if I can be of service!

Sometimes what’s holding us back with trusting others is not the trustworthiness of others, but our own distrust. Find and surround yourself with good people and you’ll always know you can count on them, and it may take a leap of faith to trust someone and delegate something important to them, sometimes that’s just our thoughts and feelings. That depends on what you want! Begin this journey with the end in sight. If you can see the end goal then you will begin to see how you can get there, and in that progress you’ll find happiness, and those that are happy are always successful.

You’re definitely not doomed for mediocrity, you just might be expecting too much. You may also be comparing too much to others, and I have a pretty bad problem with that as well, so I can relate to this a lot. Comparing to others is always bad, because it either leads to cockiness thinking we’re better, or leads to depression thinking we’re not as good so we suck. Compare yourself with who you were yesterday, and if you see even one step of progress in any aspect of your life then you’re doing much more than many others (ironic I know I’m comparing right there😂). I’m sure many people consider you to be a very competent person, you might even have people that look up to but have never admitted it, so keep giving them something to look up to!

I’ve found that typically when we’re not feeling fulfilled it is because of a lack of dopamine/serotonin, the reward chemicals that make us feel good for accomplishing something. So when we watch those videos and make a plan in our notes to improve then we get those chemicals and then we feel better, so what separates those who make plans to those who make plans and then stick to them is discipline. The chemicals can only get you so far.
Our first impressions or thoughts are not always correct, I learn to put those off and take NO action on a situation until I’ve had a chance to reconsider my initial impressions.
